rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a redundant preposition or لا, the exception follows the governed noun's syntactic case, as its substitute, rather than the preposition's surface case; the alternative wording with من is unavailable.
rows.anchor: فلما كان كذلك حمله على الموضع فجعله بدلا منه كأنه قال ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ما أنت بشيء إلا شيء, Tamim has شيء in the nominative slot while Hijaz has it accusative; when the dialects coincide, Sibawayh favors the underlying syntactic case.
rows.anchor: وبشئ في لغة أهل الحجاز في موضع منصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With لست بشيء إلا شيئا, the exception is accusative as though باء were absent; the cited line demonstrates باء before an accusative predicate.
rows.anchor: وتقول لست بشئ إلا شيئا لا يعبأ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In لا أحد فيها إلا عبد الله, the exception substitutes for the nominative مبتدأ slot; the construction answers هل من أحد, and a definite name cannot be directly coordinated with لا.
rows.anchor: لا أحد فيها إلا عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In لا أحد رأيته إلا زيد, whether رأيته is the predicate or an adjective, the analysis makes the initial noun equivalent to لا أحد مرئي or لا أحد مرئيا.
rows.anchor: رأيته إلا زيد إذا بنيت رأيته على الأول كأنك قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hijazi ما and إن cannot be reordered like verbs because they are particles; a long construction can nevertheless make otherwise difficult word order acceptable.
rows.anchor: يجز لأنهما ليسا بفعل فيحتمل قلبهما كما لم يجز فيهما التقديم والتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحد is normally confined to negation, so إن أحدا لا يقول ذاك is weak because negation follows an affirmative opening; it is tolerated when the whole sense is negative.
rows.anchor: وهو ضعيف خبيث لأن أحدا لا يستعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After إن أحدا لا يقول, إلا زيدا can substitute for the initial noun under the negative sense, or إلا زيد can attach to يقول; the latter is weaker than constructions that begin with negation.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت قلت إلا زيد فحملته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After verbs such as ظننت and وددت, أن and its clause occupy a noun phrase slot, as though the speaker said ذاك.
rows.anchor: فظننت عاملة كأنك قلت ظننت ذاك وكذلك وددت أنه ذاهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After لو or لولا, أن clauses function like ذا; Sibawayh illustrates the construction with a Quranic example and a line of poetry.
rows.anchor: فأن مبنية على لو كما كانت مبنية على لولا كأنك قلت لو ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ما رأيته مذ أن الله خلقني, أن occupies a noun slot equivalent to ذاك after مذ.
rows.anchor: مذ أن الله خلقني فقال أن في موضع اسم كأنه قال مذ

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes open أن after أما as an emphatic assertion, equivalent to حقا أنه منطلق.
rows.anchor: فسألت الخليل عن ذلك فقال إذا قال أما أنه منطلق فإنه

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes أما إنه as an alertive expression equivalent to ألا إنه ذاهب.
rows.anchor: وإذا قال أما إنه منطلق فإنه بمنزلة قوله ألا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After أما والله, open أنه conveys an assertion that the speaker knows it, while closed إنه is alertive, like ألا إنه والله.
rows.anchor: وتقول أما والله أنه ذاهب كأنك قلت قد علمت والله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ثم, open أن remains governed by the first عرفت, while closed إن starts a new statement and is no longer governed by it.
rows.anchor: قد عرفت أنه ذاهب ثم أنه معجل لأن الآخر شريك الأول في عرفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After رأيته شابا, closed إنه starts an independent clause; open وإنه is possible when the clause is attached to the verb, as in the cited poetry.
rows.anchor: رأيته شابا وإنه يفخر يومئذ كأنك قلت رأيته شابا وهذه حاله تقول

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: For 6:109, Al-Khalil rejects connecting open أنها directly to يشعركم: that would excuse the audience; he instead starts a new assertion, إنها إذا جاءت لا يؤمنون.
rows.anchor: قال لا يحسن ذا في ذا الموضع إنما

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: The people of Medina read the clause with open أنها; Al-Khalil explains their construction as لعَلَّها, meaning perhaps she will not be believed when she comes.
rows.anchor: وأهل المدينة يقولون أنها فقال الخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In إن لك هذا علي وأنك لا تؤذي, the second أن may attach to the first clause or begin independently; the cited Quranic phrase also has two readings.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت ابتدأت ولم تحمل الكلام على إن لك وقد قرئ هذا الحرف على وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group reads the Quranic clause with open وأنك, attaching it to the preceding إن لك.
rows.anchor: على إن لك وقد قرئ هذا الحرف على وجهين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another group reads the phrase with closed وإنك as a new independent statement.
rows.anchor: لا تظمأ فيها @QE@ وقال بعضهم وأنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An open أن clause is a verbal noun and does not normally follow إن or another أن directly; the sequence is avoided because it resembles competing governed nouns and clauses.
rows.anchor: ليس يحسن لأن أن تلي إن ولا أن كما قبح ابتداؤك الثقيلة المفتوحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لم أنه ظريف is expanded as an implied question and answer: قلت لمه, ثم قلت لأن ذاك كذلك.
rows.anchor: قلت لمه قلت لأن ذاك كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After أي, closed إني begins a clause meaning أنا نجد, while open أني is causal, meaning لأني نجد.
rows.anchor: أي إني نجد إذا ابتدأت كما صح أي أنا نجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some speakers lengthen kasra and damma into ياء and واو; others clip the vowels quickly while retaining their movement.
rows.anchor: فأما الذين يشبعون فيمططون وعلامتها واو وياء وهذا تحكمه لك المشافهة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Sibawayh cites Abu Amr's form إلى بارئكم in connection with the shortened-vowel pronunciation.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم قال أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vowel is still mobile in the clipped pronunciation, as shown by speakers clearly articulating the ن in من مأمنك; a silent consonant would not allow that.
rows.anchor: ويدلك على أنها متحركة قولهم من مأمنك فيبينون النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clipping does not occur in the accusative because fatḥa is lighter; its vowel measure remains, as with a hamza pronounced between full and elided forms.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون هذا في النصب لأن الفتح أخف عليهم كما لم يحذفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poets may suppress a nominative or genitive vowel by analogy with dialectal shortening in فخذ and عضد; the cited line shows the practice.
rows.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يسكنوا الحرف المرفوع والمجرور في الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rajaz line is understood as صاحبي, with the final vowel shortened in verse; the poet's informants confirmed that intended form.
rows.anchor: هذا البيت من العرب فزعم أنه يريد صاحبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh cites a line by Imru al-Qays on ishmaam, a partial rounding of the vowel, which the manuscript marks with a dot.
rows.anchor: وذلك قول الشاعر امرئ القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ishmaam pattern does not occur in the accusative, just as speakers who shorten كبد and فخذ do not use the analogous form for جمل.
rows.anchor: ولم يجيء هذا في النصب لأن الذين يقولون كبد وفخذ لا يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A masculine name of three letters without a feminine marker is fully declinable, except when its form is verb-like or begins with a verbal augment; the short masculine pattern readily bears nunation.
rows.anchor: كل مذكر سمي بثلاثة أحرف ليس فيه حرف التأنيث فهو مصروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names such as قدما and حشا remain declinable when diminutized: diminutive formation is light and no shorter pattern is available.
rows.anchor: ولو سميت رجلا قدما أو حشا صرفته فإن حقرته قلت قد نم فهو مصروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A diptote takes genitive case when annexed or when preceded by the definite article, since these contexts remove the need for nunation.
rows.anchor: إذا أضفته أو أدخلت فيه الألف واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masculine names based on بنت or أخت are declinable because their ت is part of the built name, unlike the feminine هاء; the ت behaves like that in عفريت.
rows.anchor: رجلا ببنت أو أخت صرفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A name derived from هنت becomes هنة with the ن moved and هاء retained; the rare form follows the regular pattern once made a proper name.
rows.anchor: وإن سميت رجلا بهنه وقد كانت في الوصل هنت قلت هنة يا فتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A name from ضربت becomes ضربة: four consecutive vowels are avoided, so the final ت is treated as feminine هاء.
rows.anchor: وإن سميت رجلا ضربت قلت هذا ضربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative noun after مني can be a locative, meaning the person is in a place relative to the speaker; expressions with بمنزلة الولد make this ظرف sense clear.
rows.anchor: ويدلك على أنه ظرف قولك هو منى بمنزلة الولد فإنما أردت أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Dhu'ayb's مقعد رابئ الضرباء is a place expression, located behind the star, and supports the locative construction.
rows.anchor: فوردن والعيوق مقعد رابئ الضرباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ahwas uses مناط الثريا as a locative expression for the place where the Pleiades are suspended.
rows.anchor: مناط الثريا قد تعلت نجومها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These place nouns can omit في, as in دخلت البيت and ذهبت الشأم, but this ellipsis is restricted to expressions attested in Arabic and cannot be freely used with any noun.
rows.anchor: وجاز ذلك كما جاز دخلت البيت وذهبت الشأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: درج السيل means the place where the flood ran; Ibn Hurma's درج السيول illustrates the expression, and رجع أدراجه means retracing one's route.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قول العرب هو منى درج السيل أى مكان درج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafʿ with distances, lengths of travel, and time spans states the interval between two people; فوت اليد emphasizes how close they are.
rows.anchor: وأما ما يرتفع من هذا الباب فقولك هو منى فرسخان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مرأى ومسمع is raised because it is treated as a noun for a specific place and as equivalent to the first predicate, not as a ظرف.
rows.anchor: وأما قول العرب أنت منى مرأى ومسمع فإنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh reports that some unnamed speakers use accusative مرأى ومسمع, treating it like درج السيول; this is a less common analysis.
rows.anchor: وقد زعموا أن بعض الناس ينصبه

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus reports some speakers treating مزجر الكلب, مقعد, and مناط like مرأى ومسمع, as nouns equivalent to the first predicate.
rows.anchor: مزجر الكلب يجعلونه بمنزلة مرأى ومسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poet raises the second place phrase as equivalent to the first; the construction likens the speaker's place to a tick's place on a camel.
rows.anchor: هو الأول فيجرى كقول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In دارى خلف دارك فرسخا, the accusative measure clarifies the vague distance after a complete predicate, like the specification after عشرون درهما.
rows.anchor: ما قدر ذاك فقال فرسخا وذراعا وميلا

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus reports Abu Amr's stronger analysis دارى من خلف دارك فرسخان, treating خلف as a noun; Sibawayh says Arabs also parse خلف as a predicate and use either case.
rows.anchor: وزعم يونس أن أبا عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنت مني فرسخين can be ظرف, meaning that the distance holds while the two people travel for two farsakhs.
rows.anchor: أى أنت منى ما دمنا نسير فرسخين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A time noun is accusative as a ظرف when an event occurs in it, as in القتال يوم الجمعة and الهلال الليلة; reversing order does not change that parse, while raising makes the latter noun identical with the first.
rows.anchor: وكذلك اليوم الجمعة واليوم السبت وإن شئت رفعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day names such as الأحد and الاثنين must be raised as omitted ordinal descriptions; dates like اليوم خمسة عشر من الشهر likewise mean the day completes that number.
rows.anchor: اليوم الأحد واليوم الاثنان فإنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In اليوم يومك, the first اليوم means now rather than a specific day; عهدى به قريبا or حديثا is accusative when it means recently, but raised when the second noun identifies the first.
rows.anchor: يجعل اليوم الأول بمنزلة الآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In عهدى به قائما and علمى به ذا مال, the accusatives are circumstantial predicates, not time adverbs; the same applies to ضربى عبد الله قائما.
rows.anchor: وتقول عهدى به قائما وعلمى به ذا مال فتنصب على أنه حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Time expressions are especially noun-like because they can serve as agents or patients, as in أهلكك الليل والنهار and استوفيت أيامك.
rows.anchor: تقول أهلكك الليل والنهار واستوفيت أيامك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a measure expression such as موضع كف, a partitive من is omitted before the measured material; the following accusative states its quantity or extent.
rows.anchor: ما في السماء موضع كف سحابا ولى

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil treats the genitive after the measure word as a substitute for nunation; like a tanwin it leaves the measure indefinite, and the accusative then specifies its kind.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه الله أن المجرور بدل من التنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ملء الدار, the specification may be singular or plural; the plural is allowed as with كم when it carries a collective sense like رب.
rows.anchor: في كم حين دخل فيها معنى رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line by Ka'b ibn Ju'ayl puts مرفدا in the accusative as a specification of the preceding number, illustrating the measured-noun construction.
rows.anchor: لنا مرفد سبعون ألف مدحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا كزيد فارسا is understood with an omitted noun, as though it said لا فارس كزيد فارسا, with the final accusative specifying the comparison.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك لا كزيد فارسا إذا كان الفارس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تالله رجلا is elliptical for تالله ما رأيت كاليوم رجلا or وما رأيت مثله رجلا.
rows.anchor: ما رأيت كاليوم رجلا وما رأيت مثله رجلا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says لا قولك is accusative like لا ما تقول: it stands in the slot of a relative clause and distinguishes this statement from what the addressee says.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه الله أن قوله هذا القول لا قولك إنما نصبه كنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the question أجدك لا تفعل, أجدك means أحقا, from الجد; the fixed expression retains its genitive annexation like لبيك and معاذ الله.
rows.anchor: وأصله من الجد كأنه قال أجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غير ما تقول is annexed to a known expression to reinforce the prior statement; bare غير قول would not specify which saying is meant, while غير قيل باطل is clear.
rows.anchor: غير قول أو لا قولا لم يكن فى هذا بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: البتة is only used definite; جهدك and أجهدك require annexation, whereas الحق and الباطل can be definite or indefinite because they remain fully inflected nouns like الظن and اليقين.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قولك قد قعد البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafʿ in له علم علم الفقهاء presents knowledge and related traits as established virtues and distinguishing marks, like حلم, عقل, and فضل, rather than momentary actions.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه خصال تذكرها فى الرجل كالحلم والعقل والفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative علم علم الفقهاء instead describes someone encountered while learning, before علم is an established trait; it reports an ongoing action rather than praise for a completed quality.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت نصبت فقلت له علم علم الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stable quality reading is supported by له شرف, له دين, and له فهم; unfinished qualities are expressed with verbs such as يتدين, يتشرف, and يتفهم.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه خصال تذكرها فى الرجل كالحلم والعقل والفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With له صوت صوت حمار, the accusative describes the sound made at the time of encounter; unlike knowledge, صوت is an action rather than a settled bodily quality.
rows.anchor: له صوت صوت حمار
